title: Dr Jitendra Singh announces unanimous adoption of 'Chennai Declaration', reaffirming BRICS commitment to build effective, resilient and future- ready framework in science, technology and innovation
subtitle:
Chennai Consensus places people-centred, humanity-first approach at the heart of BRICS STI cooperation; places Global South, Young Innovators and Collaborative Research at Heart of BRICS STI Agenda
BRICS Strengthens Science Partnership through Research Infrastructure, Knowledge Sharing and Innovation
body_text:
In the closing session of the 14th BRICS Science Ministerial Meet chaired by India, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science and Technology and Earth Sciences and MoS PMO, Personnel, Public Grievances, Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr Jitendra Singh announced the unanimous adoption of 'Chennai Declaration', reaffirming BRICS commitment to build effective, resilient and future- ready framework in science, technology and innovation.
The Chennai Consensus, adopted under India’s BRICS Chairship, places a people-centred and humanity-first approach at the heart of STI cooperation, with emphasis on sustainable development, resilient and high-quality growth, social inclusiveness and the use of innovation and technology to improve the welfare and quality of life of people across BRICS nations.
Delivering his closing remarks, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science and Technology and Earth Sciences and MoS PMO, Personnel, Public Grievances, Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh, said the deliberations had reaffirmed the central role of Science, Technology and Innovation in building a more resilient, inclusive and sustainable future. He said the breadth of discussions, from Artificial Intelligence and High-Performance Computing to quantum technologies, advanced materials, biotechnology, health, climate and sustainability, reflects the shared opportunities and challenges that BRICS countries can address through collective action.
The Chennai Consensus records the growing maturity and depth of BRICS STI cooperation, with sustained collaborative activity across 14 thematic Working Groups, 11 editions of the BRICS Young Scientist Forum, nine editions of the Young Innovators Prize and nine BRICS STI Framework Programme calls, including research, innovation and flagship project calls. The Declaration describes this trajectory as reflecting growing strength, investment and continued engagement in the BRICS STI partnership.
Dr. Jitendra Singh said India’s Chairship theme of “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability” must translate into concrete partnerships, stronger research networks, greater mobility of scientific talent, shared research infrastructure and more opportunities for young researchers and innovators. The Chennai Consensus also welcomes India’s efforts to review and streamline BRICS STI priorities and records the consultative work towards a more future-ready STI cooperation framework.
A major area of cooperation emerging from the Ministerial Meeting is shared research infrastructure and mega-science projects. The Chennai Consensus welcomes the outcomes of the BRICS Working Group on Research Infrastructures and Mega-science Projects, including the Action Plan and Terms of Reference for the Task Force, while also recording progress towards operationalising the BRICS Global Research Advanced Infrastructure Network (BRICS GRAIN). The framework envisages greater access to research facilities, common approaches to their use, researcher mobility and stronger collaboration around large-scale research infrastructure.
The Action Plan provides a practical framework for greater access to research infrastructure, joint research, advanced technology development, researcher mobility and capacity building, including through the BRICS Global Research Advanced Infrastructure Network (BRICS GRAIN).
The Chennai Consensus also welcomes the BRICS Science and Research Repository as a structured platform for knowledge storage and sharing among BRICS countries. Its draft framework envisages a digital public good that can map scientific institutions, researchers, research outputs, datasets, infrastructure and collaboration opportunities, while promoting knowledge exchange, open science and greater visibility of BRICS research capabilities, subject to national regulations and data governance requirements.
The people and talent dimension of BRICS STI cooperation has also received strong emphasis. The Chennai Consensus encourages greater exchanges among young scientists and welcomes continued work under the BRICS Young Scientist Forum and BRICS Young Innovator Prize. It also recognises progress under the BRICS STI Entrepreneurship Partnership towards stronger engagement among incubators, accelerators and early-stage investors, greater mobility of young innovators and researchers, and enhanced access to relevant markets.
The Declaration further welcomes the BRICS Youth Startup Platform, while recognising the need to catalyse financing for early- and growth-stage startups and recording the consideration of a BRICS Startup Innovation Fund in the BRICS Industry Ministers’ Declaration, in coordination where appropriate with the STI track.
Dr. Jitendra Singh said the BRICS STI partnership must move beyond sustained dialogue towards demonstrable outcomes, with stronger mechanisms for joint projects, shared platforms, coordinated calls and open research infrastructure. He said that as BRICS expands and evolves, its STI cooperation must remain inclusive and responsive to the priorities of the Global South, with frontier technologies becoming accessible, affordable and responsible and directed towards improving people’s lives.
The Chennai Consensus carries this approach across a wide range of emerging and strategic areas, including High-Performance Computing and Artificial Intelligence, biotechnology and human health, materials science and nanotechnology, photonics, astronomy, geospatial technologies, renewable energy, ocean and polar science, natural-disaster management and social sciences and humanities. The Declaration also welcomes continued cooperation in quantum technologies and encourages practical engagement and joint research projects among scientists, academic institutions and innovation communities.
The Ministerial Meeting also endorsed the BRICS STI Calendar of Activities for 2026–2027, providing continuity to the Working Groups, Steering Committee, Senior Officials’ process, Young Scientist Forum, Young Innovator Prize and other thematic activities. The Chennai Consensus records the transition of the BRICS STI Ministerial process to the next Chairship, with the next Ministerial Meeting scheduled under China’s Chairship in 2027.
Dr. Jitendra Singh expressed appreciation to the BRICS Ministers, delegations, experts and colleagues for their contributions to the Ministerial Meeting and acknowledged the efforts of the Department of Science and Technology and partner institutions in making India’s BRICS STI Chairship meaningful and outcome-oriented. He said the spirit of Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability should continue to guide BRICS as a platform for scientific excellence, technological progress and shared prosperity.
The adoption of the Chennai Consensus marks a significant step in strengthening BRICS STI cooperation around shared research, scientific infrastructure, innovation ecosystems, talent mobility and collaborative responses to global challenges. Under India’s Chairship, the BRICS STI partnership has been positioned for a more connected, practical and future-ready phase of cooperation, with science, technology and innovation serving as instruments of resilience, sustainable development and shared progress across the Global South.
***
NKR/AK

enrichment.summary: At the closing session of the 14th BRICS Science Ministerial Meet chaired by India in Chennai, Union Minister Dr Jitendra Singh announced the unanimous adoption of the 'Chennai Declaration' (Chennai Consensus), reaffirming BRICS commitment to a resilient, people-centred science, technology and innovation (STI) framework. The declaration endorses initiatives like the BRICS Global Research Advanced Infrastructure Network (BRICS GRAIN), a BRICS Science and Research Repository, the Young Scientist Forum, Young Innovator Prize, and a BRICS STI Calendar of Activities for 2026-27, before the chairship passes to China in 2027.
enrichment.context:
BRICS (Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa, now expanded) has run a dedicated Science, Technology and Innovation cooperation track since 2015, involving thematic Working Groups, joint research calls, and youth-focused platforms like the Young Scientist Forum and Young Innovator Prize. India held the BRICS Chairship in 2026 under the theme 'Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability,' and the Chennai Ministerial was a culmination of this chairship's STI agenda, emphasizing Global South priorities, frontier technologies (AI, quantum, biotech), and shared research infrastructure.

Such declarations are largely aspirational and consensus-building rather than binding treaties, but they matter for tracking India's soft-power positioning in South-South scientific cooperation and its attempts to shape global tech governance narratives (e.g., around AI and quantum) outside Western-led forums like G7 or OECD. Mechanisms like BRICS GRAIN and the STI Framework Programme calls represent incremental but real institutional infrastructure for researcher mobility and joint mega-science projects among BRICS nations.

prelims_questions.question: The 'Chennai Declaration' (Chennai Consensus), adopted in 2026, relates to cooperation among which group of countries?
prelims_questions.explanation: The Chennai Declaration was adopted at the 14th BRICS Science Ministerial Meet held under India's BRICS Chairship.

prelims_questions.question: Which of the following is a BRICS initiative aimed at enabling shared access to research facilities and researcher mobility, as referenced in the Chennai Consensus?
prelims_questions.explanation: BRICS GRAIN (Global Research Advanced Infrastructure Network) is the initiative for shared research infrastructure and researcher mobility mentioned in the declaration.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of multilateral science, technology and innovation cooperation platforms like BRICS STI for India's strategic and developmental goals, especially in the context of the Global South.
Examine how shared research infrastructure and researcher mobility initiatives, such as those proposed under BRICS GRAIN, can strengthen scientific capacity in developing countries.

study_notes.reason: The release names concrete, testable BRICS STI institutions and mechanisms (BRICS GRAIN, Chennai Declaration, chairship sequencing) while also offering material on India's soft-power positioning in Global South science diplomacy, giving both a factual core and analytical angle.

prelims.point: 'Chennai Declaration' (Chennai Consensus) was adopted at the 14th BRICS Science Ministerial Meet, held under India's BRICS Chairship 2026, chaired in Chennai.
prelims.why_important: UPSC frequently tests venue, chairship country and outcome-document names of multilateral summits.

prelims.point: BRICS Global Research Advanced Infrastructure Network (BRICS GRAIN) is a mechanism for shared research infrastructure and researcher mobility among BRICS nations.
prelims.why_important: A newly endorsed institutional mechanism under BRICS STI cooperation is a natural target for a factual/objective question.

prelims.point: BRICS Young Scientist Forum and BRICS Young Innovator Prize are youth-focused platforms under the BRICS STI cooperation track, running since 2015.
prelims.why_important: Distinguishing BRICS' various thematic platforms (Forum vs Prize vs Repository) is the kind of matching-based question UPSC sets.

prelims.point: India's BRICS Chairship theme for 2026 was 'Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability'; the next Ministerial will be under China's Chairship in 2027.
prelims.why_important: Chairship rotation and annual themes of BRICS are standard current-affairs factual items.

prelims.point: BRICS Science and Research Repository is proposed as a digital public good mapping scientific institutions, researchers and datasets across BRICS countries.
prelims.why_important: Tests awareness of specific new BRICS knowledge-sharing infrastructure distinct from GRAIN.

mains.point: Declarations like the Chennai Consensus are non-binding consensus statements rather than treaties, so their value lies in soft-power positioning and agenda-setting rather than enforceable commitments.
mains.analytical_use: Useful for a question on the effectiveness or limitations of BRICS as an institution, or on soft versus hard commitments in international cooperation.

mains.point: India used its BRICS Chairship to position itself as a voice for Global South priorities in frontier technology governance (AI, quantum, biotech), outside Western-led forums like G7/OECD.
mains.theme: India's science diplomacy and Global South leadership
mains.analytical_use: Deployable in questions on India's foreign policy strategy, South-South cooperation, or India's role in shaping global technology governance narratives.

mains.point: Mechanisms like BRICS GRAIN and STI Framework Programme calls represent incremental but real institutional infrastructure for joint mega-science projects and researcher mobility, moving BRICS STI cooperation from dialogue to concrete outcomes.
mains.theme: International scientific collaboration and infrastructure sharing
mains.analytical_use: Supports answers on benefits of international collaborative research infrastructure for developing countries' scientific capacity.

mains.point: The declaration emphasises frontier technologies (AI, quantum, biotech, HPC) becoming 'accessible, affordable and responsible', reflecting concerns of the Global South about technology asymmetry with developed nations.
mains.theme: Technology equity and Global South concerns
mains.analytical_use: Useful for questions on bridging the technology divide or on inclusive innovation governance frameworks.
